title: Social Post: Voter Integrity Concerns

fields.text: Breaking: Lisle County Board just confirmed 1,186 voters were falsely marked as having voted by mail. No one was deleted. But they’re saying it was a fake. Who do we believe? #LisleVotes #ElectionIntegrity

citations.documentTitle: Lisle County Board of Elections — Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan
citations.headingPath: Lisle County Board of Elections… › Section 6 › 6.4 Impersonation of the Board
citations.quote: Spoofed emails, texts or social media posts that appear to come from the Board (for example, a fake notice that a polling location moved): the PIO posts a correction within one hour on all Board chann

citations.documentTitle: Lisle County Board of Elections — Election Contingency and Continuity of Operations Plan
citations.headingPath: Lisle County Board of Elections… › Section 10
citations.quote: The PIO is the only voice of the Board to the media, with the Director. The PIO keeps a rumor log (LCBOE-F-25) and posts "Rumor vs. Fact" answers on lislevotes.example and the Board's social media acc

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. A handheld phone photo taken at an angle, slightly tilted, with flash glare on the screen. A voter in a blue Lisle County election volunteer shirt holds a paper ballot under a bright fluorescent light. The ballot shows a large red stamp in the top corner. Behind the voter, a metal door is partially closed, its cracked glass panel revealing a darkened hallway. The phone's lens is close to the ballot, focusing on the stamp. The background is blurred, but the doorVOTE HERE' sign on the wall are visible. The scene is indoors, midday, with flat overhead lighting. The voter's face is partially in shadow, looking down at the ballot. Screen is unbranded, dark except for the glowing red stamp. Setting: voters in line outside a public library used as a vote center, a VOTE HERE sign on an easel, poll workers in lanyards at the door, daylight
